deities: Lord Ganesha (Mahaganapathy - popularly the main deity)

history.dynasty: Travancore royal family tradition; major renovations in 18th and 20th centuries (per astroved.com)
history.period: Traditionally 16th century; other sources claim 10th century AD - CONFLICT (verify)
history.summary: Originally Kizhakkekara Siva Kshetram, a Shiva temple, it became famous as a Ganesha temple through a legend: the master craftsman Perumthachan carved a 3-ft Ganesha idol from a jackfruit root; refused installation at Padinjattinkara Shiva temple, he got permission at Kizhakkekara and installed it in the southeast. The priest there was preparing Unniyappam (rice-flour, coconut, ghee, sugar and kadali banana fritters); Perumthachan offered 6-7 appams strung together (Koottappam), still the favourite nivedyam, and prophesied the son would outshine the father. Dating is CONFLICTED: astroved.com says 16th century (Travancore royal family, renovations 18th/20th c.), hikollam.in claims 10th century AD. The circular sreekovil is traditionally credited to Adi Shankaracharya (verify). The temple is also famed as the place where Kerala's art form Kathakali debuted (DTPC Kollam). Note: the CSV 'state' column wrongly holds the town name 'Kollam'; actual state is Kerala.

name: Kottarakkara Ganapathy Temple
town_description: Kottarakkara is a small town in Kollam district, Kerala, about 25 km from Kollam city, on the route towards Thiruvananthapuram. A pilgrim and market town, it is best known for the Sree Mahaganapathy temple and as the traditional birthplace of Kathakali; it also serves as a halting point for Sabarimala pilgrims from the south.

travel.railway: Kottarakkara railway station (nearest); Kollam station ~25 km
travel.road: On the Kollam-Thiruvananthapuram road, ~25 km from Kollam; buses from Kollam, Trivandrum and Kottayam reach the temple

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Vinayaka Chathurthi (Chingam, Aug-Sep) for the grandest festival
